notes:
Two `[[wikilink]]` autocomplete fixes, plus tables sync merged cells across devices.

**Fixes & polish**

- **`[[ ]]` autocomplete finds your notes again.** Typing a link like `[[august]]` now surfaces the actual **august** note at the top instead of burying it under same-named journal days (*August 13th, 2026*, …). Suggestions are ranked by how well they match — exact title, then prefix, then contains — with your own notes ahead of daily-journal entries.
- **Linking a name you'd trashed no longer makes duplicates.** Before, if you'd deleted a note called "ops", typing `[[ops]]` and choosing **Create** would silently make "ops 2", then "ops 3", because the deleted note still held the name. Now it **restores the trashed note** (or reuses the existing one), so you get back the "ops" you meant — one note per name. (Also fixes a rare crash when a hidden note's name differed only by capitalization.)

**Under the hood**

- Wikilink/tag "Create" routes through a new get-or-restore-or-create path that reuses a live note, un-trashes a trashed/archived one (replicated to your other devices), or creates fresh — never a suffixed phantom. The autocomplete ranking is a pure pre-cap sort over the fetched notes. (No note data changes; pre-existing suffixed duplicates are yours to rename or merge.)
- **Merged table cells now sync cell-by-cell too.** Tables with merged cells previously fell back to whole-table last-writer-wins on a sync conflict; they now get the same convergent per-cell merge as plain grids (keyed by each cell's anchor position), so two devices editing different cells of a merged table both keep their edits. Only a genuine structural change (a concurrent merge/split) still resolves whole-table. Proven order-independent in the sync simulator. (PRD Addendum 28 §Y P5; ADR-0021.)
